In the case of a man who witnessed a sick camel being sold, and another man bought it for ten dirhams, then partnered with a man for two dirhams for the head and skin. It was judged that the camel was cured, and its value reached eight dinars. He said: 'For the owner of the two dirhams is one-fifth (khums) of what it reached. If he says,

key_terms.ضِرَار: Detriment or harm in legal context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on khums and profit distribution when partners share an asset by specific parts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in a partnership where one party invests in specific components (head and skin) and the other in the remainder, the khums of the profit belongs to the partial investor. The ruling emphasizes that demanding the physical parts instead of the monetary share constitutes *darar* (detriment/unfairness), as the khums calculation already fulfills their equitable right, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of preventing unjust enrichment in commercial partnerships.
